item.title: Roosevelt Bridge Replacement: Oklahoma starts $408m Lake Texoma span; traffic stays on old US-70
item.description: Oklahoma is set to replace the Roosevelt Bridge over Lake Texoma with a modern four-lane bridge, an ambitious project worth over $408 million. Construction has recently commenced and is expected to take about three years, with a target completion date in fall 2029. Notably, the current bridge will remain open for traffic throughout this period, enhancing safety and travel capacity across state lines.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Former Australian miner spotted Saturn ripple in 2024; two years later, co-authored 10-sided wave
item.description: An Australian amateur astronomer made a groundbreaking observation in their backyard, discovering a colossal ten-sided atmospheric wave. This unique finding corroborated the existence of a decagon around Saturn's south pole, as confirmed by years of data from the Hubble Space Telescope. The decagon, intertwined with fierce jet streams, spans numerous atmospheric levels, shedding light on the circulatory processes within the atmospheres of these gas giants.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Second Phase Of Easement: Montana pursues $17.1mn timberland deal; public can weigh in by September 26
item.description: Montana officials are proactive in their efforts to conserve approximately 48,000 acres of private timberland. This proposed conservation easement is designed to halt future development while permitting ongoing timber activities. The initiative aims to preserve wildlife habitats and maintain public access for recreation. A multimillion-dollar funding approach consists of various state and federal stakeholders, and they are currently inviting public feedback prior to making a conclusive decision.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ICE agent accused of shooting Venezuelan man arrested after 8 months
item.description: In Minneapolis, an ICE agent has been arrested due to a shooting incident in which he wounded a Venezuelan man. Facing state assault charges, the agent allegedly provided false statements to investigators about the January incident. Video footage has contradicted his claims of being attacked with household items. This arrest comes shortly after he was released on bond from federal custody earlier this month.

item.title: US farmers are turning their land into Airbnb
item.description: As farming challenges mount, many farmers are finding solace in agritourism. Brit Thompson has successfully transformed her Airstream trailer into a popular Airbnb rental, highlighting the trend's potential for financial stability. By tapping into agritourism, families can secure additional revenue streams, maintain ownership of their land, and engage in diversification that encourages resilience and opens doors to novel ventures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Britain’s butterfly boom comes with a warning for next year
item.description: Britain experienced a significant butterfly boom during the record heat of summer 2026. Over 100,000 volunteers counted nearly 1.4 million butterflies and moths across the nation. Painted ladies, a migratory species, saw their numbers surge by 335 percent this season. Experts warn this boom could lead to a population crash for caterpillars next year. Drought conditions that benefited adult butterflies harmed their offspring and food sources.

item.title: Trump to meet Gulf leaders at UN over Iran war, postwar strategy: Report
item.description: On the upcoming Tuesday, President Trump is set to convene with leaders from the Gulf region in New York, where they will strategize on the United States' plans for the post-conflict landscape in Iran. This encounter coincides with the UN General Assembly and is crucial as Gulf states navigate serious economic challenges stemming from the ongoing strife. The outcomes are expected to influence decisions post the U.S. midterms.

item.title: Syria's parliament votes to scrap Assad-era terrorism court, nullify rulings
item.description: Syria's parliament voted to abolish a counter-terrorism court established in 2012. This court was reportedly used to prosecute thousands of anti-Assad Syrians on terrorism charges. The decision formalizes the court's abolition after new authorities treated it as defunct. The United Nations Human Rights Committee had raised concerns over judicial guarantees and fair trials. This vote occurred after opposition forces removed Bashar al-Assad from power in December 2024.

item.title: In 2018, Matt Holliday paid $3M for Oklahoma land; his 62-acre estate now asks $9.8M
item.description: Former MLB star Matt Holliday's luxurious estate in Oklahoma has hit the market, boasting 62 acres of prime land including a private baseball field with professional-grade lighting. The stunning home, constructed in 2022, offers five spacious bedrooms and seven bathrooms. Among the standout features are a magnificent swimming pool and an indoor sports court. Originally listed for $12 million, it is now available for $9.8 million.

item.title: Utah couple's 14-year effort saves their 25.5-acre farm from becoming a subdivision
item.description: A couple from Utah dedicated their passion to maintaining their twenty-five-acre farm by entering into a fourteen-year conservation easement. This vital agreement safeguards the property from development, ensuring that the Schiess family's farmland remains a thriving agricultural site for future generations. By utilizing conservation easements, lands can be preserved effectively, allowing for environmental preservation without the need for public ownership.
